findings.title: deleteCache removes cache rows without checking the credential is a calendar credential
findings.body: The handler verifies ownership of the credential but then deletes all calendarCache rows for that credentialId. The UI only shows this action for Google Calendar, but the endpoint accepts any owned credential ID, so any user can wipe cache for any of their credentials. Also the access check does not limit to calendar-type credentials. Low impact but the contract is unclear.

findings.title: Credential lookup for delegation credentials may miss legitimate rows
findings.body: The ownership check uses credential.userId === user.id. Delegation credentials cached under userId in CalendarCache (in-memory delegation path) are not keyed by credentialId, so deleting by credentialId will not clear them, and the returned success is misleading to the user.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is called with an unbounded list on every connectedCalendars query
findings.body: connectedCalendarsHandler now runs a groupBy on CalendarCache for every request, including for users without the calendar-cache feature and for empty credential lists. With an empty array Prisma `in: []` still runs a query. This adds a DB round trip to a hot settings query for all users.

findings.title: updatedAt on CalendarCache is bumped on every upsert but the cache status is shown as the time of last fetch
findings.body: The Prisma field uses @updatedAt, so the timestamp reflects the last upsert. Expiry-based semantics are not captured. Combined with the migration default NOW() backfilling existing rows with the migration time, the UI will show a misleading 'last updated' for legacy caches.

findings.title: Migration backfills all existing cache rows with migration time as updatedAt
findings.body: Existing rows get updatedAt = NOW() at migration time rather than their real last-update time, so the cache status displayed for all legacy entries is incorrect until they are rewritten. The comment in the migration and schema describes this as an initial value but it misrepresents the data.

findings.title: Dropdown renders for non-Google integrations with disconnect action removed when delegated
findings.body: hasCache is only true for Google Calendar but the dropdown is rendered for every connected calendar. For a delegated credential with cache present, canDisconnect is false and the cache section still renders, which is fine, but for a non-Google credential where canDisconnect is false the component returns null so the previously shown dropdown behavior is changed. The return-null check also means the `hasCache` expression type is `Date | false | null | undefined` rather than boolean, which is a type-quality issue.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hard-coded to en-US instead of user locale
findings.body: Intl.DateTimeFormat uses 'en-US' regardless of the user's locale, so the displayed timestamp ignores the app's i18n setting even though the surrounding text is translated.

findings.title: Delete cache confirm dialog closes before mutation result
findings.body: onConfirm fires the mutation and immediately closes the dialog. The error toast is shown after the dialog closes, and the loading state is not reflected in the UI, so a failed delete gives no visible context.

findings.title: Unrelated refactor of findMany removes type-safety check
findings.body: The change drops the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` check on the args object in findMany, which weakens type checking for an unrelated reason in a feature PR.

findings.title: Writing SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all credential calendars on every cache refresh
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now calls updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}) which updates every SelectedCalendar row for the credential, including those for other event types and calendars not being refreshed. Prisma's @updatedAt will bump all of them, so updatedAt no longer means anything per calendar. Also the PR notes say this field is not displayed, so the write adds DB load for no consumer.

findings.title: Extra selected calendar fields added to session user query
findings.body: updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select on every session lookup, widening a hot query used for every authenticated request, with no consumer in the session payload shown.

findings.title: Dropdown now shown for disabled/delegated states where disconnect was previously hidden
findings.body: The previous code hid the whole actions slot when delegationCredentialId was set or disableConnectionModification was true. The new code always renders the wrapper div and passes through props, so the actions column renders an empty container in those cases and layout width changes for every calendar row.

findings.title: New deleteCache mutation and cache enrichment have no tests
findings.body: The new tRPC mutation with its ownership check, the connectedCalendars enrichment, and the new repository method are added without any unit tests, despite the PR checklist relying on manual verification only.

findings.title: sed -i '' is macOS-only syntax
findings.body: sed -i '' fails on GNU sed (Linux) and in CI containers, so the script breaks for non-macOS developers while the rest of the repo is portable. Also the script writes tunnel URLs into the shared .env without documentation.

findings.title: Cache-related strings added but the UI reuses existing keys inconsistently
findings.body: The new keys are added but the dropdown uses 'remove_app' and 'app_removed_successfully' for disconnect, and the mock/feature text says 'Delete cached data' for both the menu item and the dialog title, so the confirm dialog and trigger are indistinguishable.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without declaring tsx
findings.body: The script now relies on npx downloading tsx at run time, but tsx is not listed in devDependencies. This is unrelated to the cache feature and changes dev tooling without explanation.
